name: Rolen SyncSkin Chrome-Cover Interface Glove
description:
A slim, five-fingered glove engineered to slip over chrome hand augments and standard biological hands alike, built from a conductive graphene-weave shell with a matte charcoal finish and subtle iridescent threading. The palm is lined with a haptic mesh that reads surface texture and pressure, relaying sensation data directly to a BCI port via a thin cable routed along the dorsal seam to a magnetic snap connector at the wrist.

Fingertips can be individually detached via micro-zipper tabs — useful when the wearer has augmented digits that need direct contact. The glove cosmetically smooths the visual transition between chrome forearm and wrist, making aug-users appear more uniform in professional settings.
functionality: Haptic feedback transmits touch data to BCI. Individual fingertip removal for augmented digits. Chrome-cover profile smooths aug appearance. Magnetic wrist connector compatible with Rolen and most third-party chrome forearm ports.
what_it_says: You have chrome, you have money, and you'd prefer people not stare at the junction line.
story_hooks: A Tier 4 analyst's Rolen glove starts relaying someone else's haptic data — another user on the same BCI mesh frequency, experiencing something terrifying.
A stolen shipment of SyncSkin gloves turns up on the Shelf — modified with a secondary data-logging layer that captures every surface the wearer touches.
related_entities: Axiom Systems BCI-Integrated Mesh Network Protocol
